summary: Berbera Airport serves the historic port city of Berbera on the Gulf of Aden in northwestern Somalia. The airport supports both civilian domestic flights and military operations, and has gained strategic importance due to nearby port modernization by DP World. Its location along the coast near the Bab-el-Mandeb strait makes it a key regional aviation facility.
faqs:
Q: Does Berbera Airport offer international flights?
A: The airport primarily handles domestic flights within Somalia, with occasional regional services. International expansion has been discussed as part of broader port city development.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport has a terminal building with basic amenities, runway lighting, and parking areas, though services are limited compared to major international hubs.

Q: Is the airport safe for travelers?
A: The airport is considered one of the more stable aviation facilities in Somaliland, serving the relatively secure Berbera region.

Q: Which airlines operate from Berbera Airport?
A: Local Somali carriers such as Daallo Airlines and African Express Airways have historically operated routes connecting Berbera to other Somali cities.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers east of central Berbera, making taxi or shared transport the most common way to reach it. Road conditions on the main route are generally good, though journey times can vary. Arrange ground transport in advance, as formal rental car services are not widely available at the airport.
local_tip: Visit the nearby ruins of ancient Berbera and the Ottoman-era buildings along the coast on the same trip—the airport's proximity to the historic old town makes it easy to combine aviation travel with cultural sightseeing in one of the Horn of Africa's oldest ports.
